capabilities: Sync vault files between devices in real time over WebSocket or HTTPS
Encrypt notes, keystrokes, and file names on the device with AES-256-GCM
Edit the same open note on two devices with merged CRDT edits and per-device cursors
Pair new devices with a one-time QR code or invite code and a recovery phrase
Revoke lost devices and resolve edit-versus-delete conflicts
extras: The README warns not to run two sync tools on one vault and warns that an older plugin named Vaultbridge is a different project. Creating a vault on the hosted server requires requesting a one-time setup token from the maintainer via a GitHub issue. Limits include 25 MB per attachment and 1 MB for live-editing notes.
intentEvidence: Pick Sealed Sync for encrypted, live sync across your own devices without running a server or paying a subscription.
problem: Obsidian Sync costs money and other sync options either lack always-on end-to-end encryption, real-time merging, or need a paid plan or self-run infrastructure.

relations.evidence: Pick Obsidian Sync for the official app, version history, and support.
Pick Relay to edit live with other people.
Pick LiveSync or Remotely Save to keep the ciphertext in storage you already control.
Pick LiveSync or Remotely Save to keep the ciphertext in storage you already control.
Pick Syncthing when every device can reach the others and you want no server at all.
Edits are applied through Yjs, a CRDT.

summary: Realtime end-to-end-encrypted vault sync with live co-editing of open notes and QR-code device pairing.
